algorithms.title: Two Sum
algorithms.subtitle: Hash Map of Complements
algorithms.brief: Return indices of the two numbers adding to target. One pass, value->index map, look up target - x before storing x. LC 1, 167, 15.

algorithms.title: Prefix Sum + Hash Map
algorithms.subtitle: Subarray Sum Equals K
algorithms.brief: Count subarrays summing to k. Running prefix sum, map prefix -> count seeded {0: 1}; add count of (prefix - k) before recording prefix. Explain why a sliding window fails with negative numbers. LC 560, 523, 974, 525.

algorithms.title: Group Anagrams
algorithms.subtitle: Canonical-Key Hashing
algorithms.brief: Group words that are anagrams. Key = tuple of 26 letter counts (O(L)) vs sorted word (O(L log L)); use the count key in code, mention sorted key. Lowercase a-z input. LC 49, 242, 438.

algorithms.title: Reverse a Linked List
algorithms.subtitle: Three Pointers: prev, curr, next
algorithms.brief: Iterative reversal with prev/curr/next; mention the recursive version in prose. Python needs a ListNode class plus build_list / to_list helpers. LC 206, 92, 25.

algorithms.title: 3Sum
algorithms.subtitle: Sort, Fix One, Converge Two Pointers
algorithms.brief: All unique triplets summing to 0. Sort, fix i, left/right converge (this inner loop is Two Sum II), skip duplicates for i and after a hit. Early break when nums[i] > 0. LC 15, 167, 16, 18.

algorithms.title: Floyd's Tortoise and Hare
algorithms.subtitle: Detect a Cycle and Find Its Entry
algorithms.brief: Linked list: slow 1 step, fast 2 steps; meeting => cycle. Then reset one pointer to head, move both 1 step; they meet at the entry. Give the distance argument (a = k*c - b). Mention LC 287 (find duplicate number) and LC 202 (happy number) as the same idea on implicit lists. Python: ListNode + helper that builds a list with a cycle at a given position. LC 141, 142, 287, 202.

algorithms.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
algorithms.subtitle: Variable Window with Last-Seen Index
algorithms.brief: Map char -> last index; when a repeat is inside the window, jump left to last+1 (left never moves backward). LC 3, 159, 340, 424.

algorithms.title: Minimum Window Substring
algorithms.subtitle: Expand Right, Shrink Left
algorithms.brief: Smallest window of s containing all chars of t (with multiplicity). need-count map + 'missing' (or formed) counter; expand right, while window valid shrink left and record best. Return '' if none. LC 76, 567, 438, 30.

algorithms.title: Binary Search
algorithms.subtitle: The Lower-Bound Template
algorithms.brief: Half-open [lo, hi) template returning the first index i with a[i] >= target (len(a) if none). Derive exact search, upper bound (first > target), insert position and first/last occurrence from it. Explain the loop invariant. Write it by hand (bisect only mentioned). LC 704, 35, 34, 278.

algorithms.title: Binary Search on the Answer
algorithms.subtitle: Search a Monotone Yes/No Predicate
algorithms.brief: Koko Eating Bananas as the example: smallest speed s in [1, max(piles)] with hours(s) <= h. feasible(x) is monotone so binary search for the first True. Show the general shape (lo/hi = answer range, check function). LC 875, 1011, 410, 1482.

algorithms.title: Merge Sort
algorithms.subtitle: Divide, Sort Halves, Merge
algorithms.brief: Top-down merge sort returning a new list; merge with <= for stability. Explain the recursion tree (log n levels, O(n) work per level). Mention counting inversions as the classic extension. LC 912, 148, 315, 493.

algorithms.title: Quick Sort
algorithms.subtitle: Partition Around a Random Pivot
algorithms.brief: In-place quick sort with Lomuto partition and a random pivot (swap it to the end). Explain the partition invariant [lo..store-1] < pivot. Worst case O(n^2) on bad pivots and why randomizing helps; not stable. Mention Hoare partition in prose. LC 912, 215, 75.

algorithms.title: Top-K Elements
algorithms.subtitle: Keep a Size-K Min-Heap
algorithms.brief: k largest values / kth largest: push each value, pop when size > k; the heap top is the kth largest. O(n log k). Mention K Closest Points as the same pattern with a distance key and a max-heap by negation. LC 215, 347, 973, 703.

algorithms.title: Merge K Sorted Arrays
algorithms.subtitle: A Heap of the Front Elements
algorithms.brief: Heap of (value, array index, element index); pop smallest, push its successor. O(N log k). Mention the linked-list version (LC 23) and kth smallest in sorted matrix. LC 23, 378, 632, 373.

algorithms.title: Find Median from Data Stream
algorithms.subtitle: Two Heaps Meet in the Middle
algorithms.brief: MedianFinder class: low = max-heap (negated values) holding the smaller half, high = min-heap; add pushes through low into high then rebalance so len(low) >= len(high) by at most 1; median from tops. LC 295, 480, 502.

algorithms.title: Valid Parentheses
algorithms.subtitle: The Matching Stack
algorithms.brief: Brackets ()[]{}: push openers, on a closer the top must be its partner; valid iff stack empty at the end. LC 20, 1249, 921, 32.

algorithms.title: Monotonic Stack
algorithms.subtitle: Next Greater Element
algorithms.brief: Daily Temperatures form: for each day, days until a warmer one (0 if none). Stack of indices whose temperatures decrease; a warmer day pops and answers everyone it beats. Each index pushed/popped once => O(n). Mention previous-smaller and circular variants. LC 739, 496, 503, 901.

algorithms.title: Merge Intervals
algorithms.subtitle: Sort by Start, Sweep and Extend
algorithms.brief: Sort by start; if next start <= last end then extend last end with max, else append. Closed intervals ([1,4],[4,5] merge). Mention Insert Interval (LC 57) as the no-sort version. LC 56, 57, 986, 252.

algorithms.title: Meeting Rooms II
algorithms.subtitle: Minimum Rooms with a Heap of End Times
algorithms.brief: Half-open [start, end): sort by start, min-heap of end times; if earliest end <= start reuse that room (pop) then push the new end; answer = max heap size (or final size). Also explain the sweep-line +1/-1 events view (ends sorted before starts at equal times) in prose. LC 253, 1094, 2406, 732.

algorithms.title: Kadane's Algorithm
algorithms.subtitle: Maximum Subarray: Extend or Restart
algorithms.brief: best ending here = max(x, ending_here + x); global best. Handles all-negative arrays (do not start best at 0). Show how to recover the subarray bounds in prose or code. LC 53, 918, 152, 1749.

algorithms.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
algorithms.subtitle: Track the Running Minimum
algorithms.brief: One transaction: profit = price - min so far. Mention the unlimited-transactions variant (sum of positive day-to-day rises) in prose. LC 121, 122, 714, 309.

algorithms.title: Subsets
algorithms.subtitle: Choose, Recurse, Un-Choose
algorithms.brief: Start-index backtracking: record a copy of path at every node, loop i from start, append, recurse(i+1), pop. 2^n subsets. Mention duplicates handling (sort + skip nums[i] == nums[i-1] when i > start) for LC 90. LC 78, 90, 1863.

algorithms.title: Permutations
algorithms.subtitle: Backtracking with a Used Array
algorithms.brief: used[] booleans; when path length == n record a copy; try every unused element. n! leaves. Mention duplicates (sort + skip if same as previous and previous unused) for LC 47. LC 46, 47, 31.

algorithms.title: Binary Tree Level-Order Traversal
algorithms.subtitle: BFS One Level at a Time
algorithms.brief: Queue; snapshot len(queue) to process exactly one level per outer loop; return list of levels. Mention right side view and zigzag as variants. Python needs TreeNode + build_tree from a level-order list with None. LC 102, 199, 103, 637.

algorithms.title: Diameter and Max Path Sum
algorithms.subtitle: Postorder DFS That Returns a Height
algorithms.brief: Pattern: the recursive call returns the best downward path (height / gain) while the answer through the current node (left + right) updates a global best. Show diameter first (edges), then max path sum with gains clipped at 0 (handles negatives). Python: two functions, best tracked in a one-element list or returned as a pair. LC 543, 124, 110, 687.

algorithms.title: Lowest Common Ancestor
algorithms.subtitle: Postorder Search in a Binary Tree
algorithms.brief: Return the node if it is p or q or null; recurse left and right; if both non-null the current node is the LCA, else pass up the non-null one. Assume both nodes exist. Mention the BST split-point version (LC 235) and parent-pointer version. LC 236, 235, 1650.

algorithms.title: Validate a Binary Search Tree
algorithms.subtitle: Carry the Allowed Range Down
algorithms.brief: Recurse with (low, high) bounds, strict inequalities; left child gets high = node.val, right gets low = node.val. Mention the inorder-must-be-strictly-increasing alternative and why checking only parent vs child fails. LC 98, 230.

algorithms.title: Depth-First Search on a Graph
algorithms.subtitle: Recursive and Iterative
algorithms.brief: Adjacency list (dict or list of lists), visited set marked on entry. Show recursive DFS and the iterative stack version (mark when popped, or when pushed - explain which gives true DFS order). Return visit order. Mention recursion depth limits. LC 547, 841, 797, 133.

algorithms.title: Number of Islands
algorithms.subtitle: Grid Flood Fill
algorithms.brief: Scan cells; each unvisited '1' starts a DFS that sinks/marks the whole island; count starts. Show 4-directional neighbors. Use an explicit stack in code to avoid recursion limits (mention recursive form). LC 200, 695, 733, 130.

algorithms.title: BFS Shortest Path
algorithms.subtitle: Unweighted Graphs, Layer by Layer
algorithms.brief: dist map / array, mark visited when enqueued (not when dequeued); first time a node is reached is its shortest distance; keep parent pointers to rebuild the path. Example on an adjacency list; mention grid version (LC 1091). LC 1091, 1971, 433, 286.

algorithms.title: Kahn's Algorithm
algorithms.subtitle: Topological Sort by Peeling Indegree-Zero Nodes
algorithms.brief: Indegrees, queue of indegree-0 nodes, pop -> append to order -> decrement neighbors -> enqueue new zeros. If order has fewer than n nodes there is a cycle. Course Schedule II framing (prerequisite pairs [a, b] mean b -> a). LC 207, 210, 269, 1136.

algorithms.title: Union-Find
algorithms.subtitle: Path Compression + Union by Size
algorithms.brief: DSU class: parent, size, find with path compression (iterative or recursive), union returns False if already connected, count of components. Near O(1) amortized (inverse Ackermann). Example: count components and find a redundant edge. LC 684, 547, 323, 721.

algorithms.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
algorithms.subtitle: Shortest Paths with Non-Negative Weights
algorithms.brief: Min-heap of (dist, node), lazy deletion: skip popped entries whose dist > best known. Relax edges. Explain why negative edges break it. Network Delay Time framing. O((V + E) log V). LC 743, 1514, 1631, 1976.

algorithms.title: Trie
algorithms.subtitle: Insert, Search, Starts With
algorithms.brief: TrieNode with children dict + is_end flag; insert/search/starts_with all O(L). Mention autocomplete and wildcard search ('.' DFS, LC 211) in prose. LC 208, 211, 1268, 648.

algorithms.title: LRU Cache
algorithms.subtitle: Hash Map + Doubly Linked List
algorithms.brief: Map key -> node; doubly linked list with head/tail sentinels, most recent next to head; get moves to front; put inserts/moves to front and evicts the node before tail when over capacity. All O(1). Implement the list by hand; mention OrderedDict in prose. LC 146, 460.

algorithms.title: Hash Map with Separate Chaining
algorithms.subtitle: Collisions Live in Buckets
algorithms.brief: Array of buckets, each a list of [key, value] pairs; index = hash(key) mod capacity; a collision is two keys in the same bucket and is resolved by comparing keys inside the bucket; put/get/remove; resize (double + rehash every pair) when size / capacity > 0.75. Explain load factor and why average O(1), worst O(n). LC 706, 705.

algorithms.title: Trapping Rain Water
algorithms.subtitle: Two Pointers with Running Walls
algorithms.brief: water at i = min(max left, max right) - height[i]. Two pointers: the side with the lower running max is settled, so move it. Mention prefix/suffix max arrays (O(n) space) and Container With Most Water (LC 11) as a cousin. LC 42, 11, 407.

algorithms.title: Dutch National Flag
algorithms.subtitle: Three-Way Partition in One Pass
algorithms.brief: Sort 0/1/2 in place: low, mid, high pointers; 0 swap to low (advance both), 1 advance mid, 2 swap to high (do not advance mid). Invariant regions. Tie to 3-way quicksort partition. LC 75, 905, 2161.

algorithms.title: Search in a Rotated Sorted Array
algorithms.subtitle: One Half Is Always Sorted
algorithms.brief: Distinct values: compare nums[lo] <= nums[mid] to find the sorted half, check if target lies inside it, discard the other half. Mention finding the minimum (LC 153) and duplicates (LC 81) in prose. LC 33, 153, 81.

algorithms.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
algorithms.subtitle: Binary Search the Partition
algorithms.brief: Binary search a cut i in the shorter array, j = (m + n + 1) // 2 - i; valid when A[i-1] <= B[j] and B[j-1] <= A[i] with -inf/+inf at the edges. O(log min(m, n)). Mention the merge brute force O(m + n). LC 4.

algorithms.title: Heapify
algorithms.subtitle: Build a Heap in O(n) with Sift-Down
algorithms.brief: Array min-heap: children 2i+1, 2i+2, parent (i-1)//2. sift_down; heapify by sifting down from n//2 - 1 to 0. Explain why it is O(n) (most nodes are near the bottom; sum of heights). Also sift_up for push and pop = swap root with last + sift_down. Python by hand; demo can compare with heapq. LC 912, 215, 1046.

algorithms.title: Quickselect
algorithms.subtitle: Kth Largest in Expected O(n)
algorithms.brief: Partition with a random pivot (Lomuto), then continue only into the side holding target index n - k; loop instead of recursion. Expected O(n), worst O(n^2). Compare with the heap approach (#13). LC 215, 973, 347.

algorithms.title: Bucket Sort
algorithms.subtitle: Top K Frequent by Frequency Buckets
algorithms.brief: Count frequencies; bucket[f] = values with frequency f (f in 0..n); walk buckets from n down collecting k values. O(n). Explain general bucket sort (values spread over ranges, sort each bucket) in prose. LC 347, 451, 692, 164.

algorithms.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
algorithms.subtitle: Monotonic Increasing Stack
algorithms.brief: Stack of indices with increasing heights; when a shorter bar arrives, pop: popped bar's rectangle spans from the new stack top + 1 to i - 1. Append a 0 sentinel to flush. Mention maximal rectangle in a matrix (LC 85). LC 84, 85, 1793.

algorithms.title: Basic Calculator
algorithms.subtitle: Evaluate + - * / and Parentheses with a Stack
algorithms.brief: Expression of non-negative ints, + - * /, parentheses, spaces; '/' truncates toward zero. Per level: stack of signed terms with the previous operator (+ push, - push negative, * / combine with top); '(' recurses with an index and returns (value, next index). Unary minus at start or after '(' works because the initial op is '+'. LC 224, 227, 772, 150.

algorithms.title: Sliding Window Maximum
algorithms.subtitle: Monotonic Deque
algorithms.brief: Deque of indices with decreasing values: pop back while smaller than the new value, pop front if it left the window, front is the max. O(n). LC 239, 1438, 862, 1696.

algorithms.title: Jump Game
algorithms.subtitle: Track the Farthest Reach
algorithms.brief: Scan i while i <= farthest; farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i]); reachable if farthest >= n - 1. LC 55, 45, 1306.

algorithms.title: Jump Game II
algorithms.subtitle: Greedy BFS over Reach Levels
algorithms.brief: Minimum jumps: current_end of this jump's reach, farthest seen; when i hits current_end, jumps += 1 and current_end = farthest. Explain it as BFS where each level is an interval. Assume the end is reachable. LC 45, 1024, 1326.

algorithms.title: Gas Station
algorithms.subtitle: Restart After Every Deficit
algorithms.brief: If total gas < total cost return -1; otherwise scan with a tank, and when the tank goes negative the start moves to i + 1 and tank resets. Argue why no station in the failed stretch can be a start. LC 134.

algorithms.title: Interval Scheduling
algorithms.subtitle: Sort by End, Keep What Fits
algorithms.brief: Maximum number of non-overlapping intervals (and min removals = n - kept). Sort by end; keep an interval if its start >= last kept end. Exchange argument for why earliest end is safe. LC 435, 452, 646, 1353.

algorithms.title: Task Scheduler
algorithms.subtitle: Frame the Most Frequent Task
algorithms.brief: Least intervals with cooldown n: max_count frames (max_count - 1) * (n + 1) + number of tasks tied at max_count; answer = max(that, len(tasks)). Explain the grid picture. Mention heap simulation and Reorganize String (LC 767). LC 621, 767, 358.

algorithms.title: Partition Labels
algorithms.subtitle: Extend to the Last Occurrence
algorithms.brief: last[c] for each char; scan extending end = max(end, last[c]); when i == end cut a part. Return part sizes. LC 763, 56.

algorithms.title: Combination Sum
algorithms.subtitle: Unlimited Reuse with a Start Index
algorithms.brief: Distinct positive candidates, reuse allowed: sort, recurse with start = i (not i + 1) to allow reuse, stop when remaining < candidate (pruning thanks to sorting). Mention LC 40 (each once, skip duplicates) and LC 216. LC 39, 40, 216, 377.

algorithms.title: Word Search
algorithms.subtitle: Grid Backtracking with In-Place Marks
algorithms.brief: For each cell start a DFS matching word[k]; mark the cell visited (e.g. '#'), recurse 4 ways, restore. O(m * n * 4^L) worst case. Mention pruning with letter counts. LC 79, 212.

algorithms.title: Serialize and Deserialize a Binary Tree
algorithms.subtitle: Preorder with Null Markers
algorithms.brief: Preorder with '#' for null, comma separated; deserialize by reading tokens with a moving index (recursive helper taking the token list and a one-element index holder or returning (node, next_index)). Explain why null markers make preorder alone unambiguous. LC 297, 449, 105.

algorithms.title: BST Search, Insert, Delete
algorithms.subtitle: Delete with the In-Order Successor
algorithms.brief: Search (iterative), insert (recursive, return root), delete with three cases: leaf, one child, two children (copy successor = leftmost of right subtree, then delete it from the right subtree). O(h). LC 700, 701, 450.

algorithms.title: BST Iterator
algorithms.subtitle: Controlled In-Order with a Stack
algorithms.brief: Class: push the left chain; next() pops, then pushes the left chain of the popped node's right child; has_next() = stack not empty. O(1) amortized, O(h) space. Kth smallest = call next() k times. LC 173, 230, 285, 1305.

algorithms.title: Multi-Source BFS
algorithms.subtitle: Rotting Oranges
algorithms.brief: Grid 0 empty, 1 fresh, 2 rotten: enqueue all rotten at time 0, BFS by levels, count fresh; return minutes or -1 if fresh remain. Explain why starting from all sources at once gives each cell its nearest-source distance. LC 994, 542, 286, 1162.

algorithms.title: Word Ladder
algorithms.subtitle: BFS on an Implicit Graph
algorithms.brief: Return number of words in the shortest transformation sequence (0 if none). Build wildcard buckets ('h*t' -> words) or try 26 letters per position; BFS from begin word. Mention bidirectional BFS as an optimization. LC 127, 126, 752, 433.

algorithms.title: Cycle Detection in a Directed Graph
algorithms.subtitle: Three Colors: White, Gray, Black
algorithms.brief: DFS with colors: white unvisited, gray on the current path, black finished; an edge to a gray node is a back edge = cycle. Explain why a plain visited set is not enough in directed graphs. Mention Kahn's count check (#31) as the BFS alternative. LC 207, 802, 1059.

algorithms.title: Topological Sort with DFS
algorithms.subtitle: Reverse Postorder
algorithms.brief: DFS with three colors; append a node after all its descendants finish; reverse the finished list. Return [] if a gray node is reached (cycle). Compare with Kahn's (#31). LC 210, 269, 1203, 329.

algorithms.title: Connected Components
algorithms.subtitle: Count and Label by Flood Fill
algorithms.brief: n nodes 0..n-1 and an undirected edge list: build adjacency, iterate nodes, each unvisited node starts a DFS/BFS that labels its component; return count (and labels). Mention union-find (#32) when edges arrive online. LC 323, 547, 1971, 2316.

algorithms.title: Word Search II
algorithms.subtitle: Trie-Guided Grid Backtracking
algorithms.brief: Insert all words into a trie (store the word at its end node); DFS from each cell following trie children; on reaching a stored word record it and clear it to avoid duplicates; prune leaf nodes optionally. Explain why one trie walk beats searching each word. LC 212, 79.

algorithms.title: KMP String Matching
algorithms.subtitle: The Prefix Function Never Re-Reads the Text
algorithms.brief: lps[i] = length of the longest proper prefix of pattern[0..i] that is also a suffix; build it with the fallback j = lps[j - 1]; search with the same loop; return all match start indices. O(n + m). LC 28, 1392, 459, 214.

algorithms.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
algorithms.subtitle: Expand Around Every Center
algorithms.brief: 2n - 1 centers (each char and each gap); expand while ends match; keep the best. O(n^2) time, O(1) space. Mention counting palindromic substrings (LC 647) and Manacher's O(n) in prose. LC 5, 647, 516.

algorithms.title: Encode and Decode Strings
algorithms.subtitle: Length-Prefix Framing
algorithms.brief: Encode each string as len + '#' + s; decode by reading digits up to '#', then exactly len characters. Works for strings containing '#' or digits; explain why delimiter-only schemes break. LC 271, 535.

algorithms.title: Fibonacci
algorithms.subtitle: Recursion, Memo, Iteration, Fast Doubling
algorithms.brief: F(0)=0, F(1)=1. Show the exponential recursion tree, memoization O(n), two-variable iteration O(1) space, and fast doubling O(log n): F(2k) = F(k) * (2F(k+1) - F(k)), F(2k+1) = F(k)^2 + F(k+1)^2. Mention climbing stairs as the same recurrence. LC 509, 70, 1137.

algorithms.title: Single Number
algorithms.subtitle: XOR Cancels Pairs
algorithms.brief: x ^ x = 0, x ^ 0 = x, XOR is commutative: XOR everything to find the element that appears once. Also missing number 0..n by XOR-ing indices and values. Mention two singles (LC 260, split by lowest set bit). LC 136, 268, 389, 260.

algorithms.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
algorithms.subtitle: Array + Index Map, Swap with Last
algorithms.brief: values list + value -> index map; remove swaps the target with the last element, fixes the moved element's index, pops. get_random picks a random index. Demo must be deterministic: seed random or print only membership/size results. LC 380, 381.

algorithms.title: Time-Based Key-Value Store
algorithms.subtitle: Per-Key Timestamp Lists + Binary Search
algorithms.brief: set(key, value, t) with increasing t per key appends (t, value); get(key, t) binary searches the last timestamp <= t ('' if none). Write the binary search by hand (upper bound - 1). LC 981, 1146.

algorithms.title: Hash Map with Open Addressing
algorithms.subtitle: Linear Probing and Tombstones
algorithms.brief: One array of slots; probe index, index + 1, ... (mod capacity) until the key or an EMPTY slot; delete leaves a DELETED tombstone so later probes keep going; put reuses the first tombstone seen; resize (double, reinsert live keys) when (size + tombstones) / capacity > 0.5. Collision = occupied slot with another key. Explain primary clustering. LC 706, 705.

algorithms.title: Boyer-Moore Majority Vote
algorithms.subtitle: Different Votes Cancel in Pairs
algorithms.brief: candidate + count: count 0 -> adopt x; same -> +1; different -> -1. Second pass verifies when a majority is not guaranteed. Mention the n/3 version with two candidates (LC 229). LC 169, 229, 1150.

algorithms.title: Median of K Sorted Arrays
algorithms.subtitle: Binary Search on the Value
algorithms.brief: Integers, total N >= 1. Brute force in prose: heap-merge (#14) up to the middle, O(N log k). Optimal: kth_smallest(k) = smallest value v in [min, max] with count(<= v) >= k, where count sums an upper-bound binary search over each array; median = kth(N//2 + 1) for odd N, average of kth(N//2) and kth(N//2 + 1) for even. O(k log L log R). bisect allowed (binary search chapter) but a hand-written upper bound is clearer. LC 4, 378, 719, 668.

algorithms.title: Counting Sort
algorithms.subtitle: Count, Prefix-Sum, Place
algorithms.brief: Integers in a small range [min, max]: counts with offset (handles negatives), prefix sums give final positions, place from the right for stability. O(n + k). Mention radix sort (counting sort per digit) in prose. LC 912, 1051, 274, 164.

algorithms.title: Heap Sort
algorithms.subtitle: Build a Max-Heap, Swap the Max to the End
algorithms.brief: In place: build a max-heap with sift-down from n//2 - 1 (see #41, max version), then repeatedly swap a[0] with a[end] and sift down within [0, end). O(n log n) worst case, O(1) space, not stable. LC 912, 215.

algorithms.title: Circular Queue
algorithms.subtitle: Ring Buffer with Head and Count
algorithms.brief: Fixed array, head index and count; tail = (head + count) % capacity; enqueue/dequeue/front/rear/is_empty/is_full all O(1) with wrap-around by modulo. LC 622, 641, 346.

algorithms.title: Candy
algorithms.subtitle: Two Passes: Left, Then Right
algorithms.brief: Everyone gets 1; left-to-right gives more than a lower left neighbor; right-to-left takes max with right neighbor + 1. Sum. Explain why each pass enforces one side's constraint without breaking the other. LC 135, 2398.

algorithms.title: Hand of Straights
algorithms.subtitle: Start Every Group at the Smallest Card
algorithms.brief: Count map; iterate distinct cards in sorted order; while the smallest card has count c > 0 it must start c groups: subtract c from the next group_size - 1 consecutive cards (fail if short). O(n log n). LC 846, 1296, 659.

algorithms.title: N-Queens
algorithms.subtitle: Columns and Diagonals as Sets
algorithms.brief: Place one queen per row; sets for columns, r - c diagonals and r + c anti-diagonals give O(1) safety checks; build boards as lists of strings. Mention counting only (LC 52). LC 51, 52, 37.

algorithms.title: Bipartite Check
algorithms.subtitle: BFS Two-Coloring
algorithms.brief: graph as adjacency list (LC 785 format); color each uncolored node 0 and BFS, giving neighbors the opposite color; same-colored neighbors => not bipartite. Handle disconnected graphs. Equivalent: no odd cycle. LC 785, 886, 1042.

algorithms.title: Cycle Detection in an Undirected Graph
algorithms.subtitle: DFS That Skips the Parent Edge
algorithms.brief: Iterative or recursive DFS carrying the parent; meeting a visited node that is not the parent => cycle. Handle disconnected graphs. Mention union-find (#32): an edge whose ends are already connected closes a cycle; mention Graph Valid Tree (n - 1 edges + connected). Simple graphs (no parallel edges). LC 261, 684, 1559.

algorithms.title: Bellman-Ford
algorithms.subtitle: Relax Every Edge n - 1 Times
algorithms.brief: dist[src] = 0; repeat n - 1 rounds relaxing every edge (stop early if nothing changed); one more round that still relaxes => negative cycle reachable. O(V * E). Mention the K-stops variant (LC 787) that relaxes from a copy of the previous round. LC 787, 743, 1334.

algorithms.title: Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree
algorithms.subtitle: Sort Edges, Let Union-Find Reject Cycles
algorithms.brief: Sort edges by weight; add an edge if union-find joins two different components; stop at n - 1 edges. Cut property explanation. Include a compact DSU (see #32). Return total weight and edges (or -1 / None if disconnected). LC 1584, 1135, 1489.

algorithms.title: Prim's Minimum Spanning Tree
algorithms.subtitle: Grow One Tree with a Min-Heap
algorithms.brief: Start at node 0; min-heap of (weight, node); pop, skip if already in tree, else add weight and push its edges to outside nodes. O(E log V). Mention the O(V^2) array version for dense graphs (Min Cost to Connect All Points). LC 1584, 1135.

algorithms.title: Rabin-Karp
algorithms.subtitle: Rolling Hash Pattern Matching
algorithms.brief: Polynomial hash with base 256 (or 131) mod a large prime; roll: remove leading char * base^(m-1), multiply by base, add new char; on hash equality verify the substring to rule out collisions. Expected O(n + m). Mention repeated DNA sequences and longest duplicate substring (binary search + rolling hash). LC 28, 187, 1044, 1316.

algorithms.title: Longest Common Prefix
algorithms.subtitle: Vertical Scan
algorithms.brief: Compare column by column across all strings, stop at the first mismatch or the end of the shortest string. O(total characters). Mention sorting and comparing only first and last, and the trie view. LC 14, 1408.

algorithms.title: Text Justification
algorithms.subtitle: Greedy Line Packing, Then Spread the Spaces
algorithms.brief: Pack as many words as fit (word lengths + one gap each); full lines spread spaces evenly with the extra going to the leftmost gaps; a single-word line and the last line are left-justified and padded. LC 68.

algorithms.title: String Compression
algorithms.subtitle: Run-Length Encoding with Read and Write Pointers
algorithms.brief: LC 443: compress a char list in place ('a','a','b' -> 'a','2','b'), counts > 1 written digit by digit, return new length. Read pointer scans runs, write pointer writes. Mention decoding. LC 443, 38, 271.

algorithms.title: Reverse Words in a String
algorithms.subtitle: Reverse All, Then Reverse Each Word
algorithms.brief: Show the in-place trick on a char array: reverse the whole array, then reverse each word; also collapse extra spaces (LC 151 trims and single-spaces). Python: work on a list of chars with a reverse(chars, i, j) helper; mention split/join as the library shortcut. LC 151, 186, 557.

algorithms.title: Multiply Strings
algorithms.subtitle: Grade-School Multiplication into a Digit Array
algorithms.brief: Result array of m + n digits; digit i of a times digit j of b lands at position i + j + 1 with carry to i + j; strip leading zeros, '0' special case. Mention Add Strings (LC 415) and Add Binary (LC 67) carry loops. LC 43, 415, 67.

algorithms.title: GCD and LCM
algorithms.subtitle: Euclid's Algorithm
algorithms.brief: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b), gcd(a, 0) = a; lcm = a // gcd(a, b) * b; gcd of a list. Explain why it is O(log min(a, b)). Mention GCD of strings (LC 1071) and fraction reduction (used by #97). LC 1979, 1071, 914, 2413.

algorithms.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
algorithms.subtitle: Cross Out Multiples Starting at p squared
algorithms.brief: Count/list primes < n: boolean array, for p from 2 while p * p < n, if prime cross out p*p, p*p+p, ...; O(n log log n). Also trial division up to sqrt(n) for a single number. LC 204, 2523, 952.

algorithms.title: Fast Exponentiation
algorithms.subtitle: Square and Multiply
algorithms.brief: Iterative binary exponentiation: while e > 0, if e odd multiply result by base, square base, halve e. O(log e). Handle negative exponents for pow(x, n) and show the modular version. LC 50, 372, 1922.

algorithms.title: Reservoir Sampling
algorithms.subtitle: Keep the i-th Item with Probability k / i
algorithms.brief: Sample k items uniformly from a stream of unknown length: fill the reservoir with the first k, then for item i (1-based) pick j = random int in [1, i], replace reservoir[j - 1] if j <= k. Prove uniformity for k = 1 (telescoping product). Demo must be deterministic: e.g. run many trials with a seed and print whether every count is within a tolerance (True). LC 382, 398, 497.

algorithms.title: Orientation and Segment Intersection
algorithms.subtitle: The Cross Product Decides Left or Right
algorithms.brief: cross(o, a, b) = (a.x - o.x)(b.y - o.y) - (a.y - o.y)(b.x - o.x): > 0 left turn (counter-clockwise), < 0 right turn, 0 collinear. Segments p1p2 and q1q2 intersect iff orientations straddle both ways, plus on-segment checks for collinear touching cases. Integer coordinates. Used by #96. LC 587, 1232, 2280.

algorithms.title: Convex Hull
algorithms.subtitle: Andrew's Monotone Chain
algorithms.brief: Sort points by (x, y); build the lower hull left to right popping while the last turn is not counter-clockwise (cross <= 0), build the upper hull right to left the same way, concatenate without repeated endpoints. O(n log n). Note: LC 587 (Erect the Fence) wants collinear boundary points kept: pop only when cross < 0 and de-duplicate. LC 587, 1924.

algorithms.title: Max Points on a Line
algorithms.subtitle: Slopes as Reduced Fractions
algorithms.brief: For each anchor point, count other points by slope key (dy // g, dx // g) normalized so dx > 0, or (1, 0) for vertical lines; the best line through the anchor = max count + 1. Avoid floating slopes. Distinct points (as in LC 149). O(n^2). LC 149, 1232, 2280.

algorithms.title: Count Set Bits
algorithms.subtitle: Brian Kernighan's n & (n - 1)
algorithms.brief: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit, so the loop runs once per set bit; power of two iff n > 0 and n & (n - 1) == 0; lowest set bit n & -n; counting bits 0..n with bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1). Non-negative ints. LC 191, 231, 338, 461.

algorithms.title: Bitmask Subset Enumeration
algorithms.subtitle: Every Integer from 0 to 2^n - 1 Is a Subset
algorithms.brief: Bit j of mask says whether element j is in; loop mask over 0..2^n - 1 to list all subsets; iterate submasks of a mask with sub = (sub - 1) & mask. Compare with backtracking subsets (#22). LC 78, 2044, 1178.

algorithms.title: Rate Limiter
algorithms.subtitle: Token Bucket and Sliding Log
algorithms.brief: Token bucket class: capacity, refill rate per second, tokens refilled lazily from elapsed time on each allow(t) call; allow if tokens >= 1. Sliding log class: deque of timestamps, drop those older than window, allow if fewer than limit (LC 359 / 362 style). Callers pass timestamps so demos are deterministic. Discuss trade-offs (burst vs smoothness, memory). LC 359, 362, 1396.
